# Biocompression Arterial Pump

[Pumps, ][42]
[ « View All Compression Device Products][43]

Bio Arterial Plus is an Intermittent, Sequential, Pneumatic Compression System that sequentially
compresses the lower extremity in patients suffering primarily from arterial ulcers, ischemia or
intermittent claudication (leg pain primarily from decreased arterial circulation). The BIOARTERIAL
PLUS SYSTEM is designed to deliver pressures of 120mmHg for two to three treatments per day. The
BIOARTERIAL PLUS SYSTEM increases arterial blood flow in both the popliteal artery and at the tissue
level. Substantial blood flow increases were realized through duplex ultrasonic imaging of the
popliteal artery following treatment with the BIOARTERIAL PLUS. Through affective compression,
resultant evacuation of venous blood from the lower limbs, enables replacement with substantial
volumes of oxygenated arterial blood.

# Calibrated Pneumatic Compression Device

[Pumps, ][42]
[ « View All Compression Device Products][43]

This model has additional features that allow the user to program the pressure setting in any and
all of the 8 chambers, always keeping greater pressure distal so as to avoid any reflux. Complete
with a compliance meter to monitor patient use, the SC-3008-DL also has a countdown clock and a
timer that shuts off the pump after one hour.

## CONTRAINDICATIONS

Use of this device is contraindicated for patients with the following condition:
1. Congestive heart failure
2. Deep Vein Thrombosis
3. Inflammatory phlebitis or episodes of pulmonary embolism
4. Infections in the limb, including cellulitis without appropriate antibiotic coverage
5. Presence of cancer unless for palliative care (By order of a physician only)

# Sequential Pneumatic Compression Device

[Pumps, ][42]
[ « View All Compression Device Products][43]

A widely recognized and highly effective treatment is using a compression pump. This is a safe and
effective way to assist your body’s circulatory system in moving the excess fluid which has
accumulated in the limb and can cause painful swelling, non-healing wounds, heaviness, and
discomfort decreasing your mobility. The compression pump is a gentle massaging technique that
compresses in a rhythmic cycle, similar to that of a normally functioning lymphatic system that has
not been damaged. This is a great treatment option for patients who have tried compression stocking,
elevation, diuretics, or massage with little or no relief.

## Key Patient Benefits
* Reduces Pain
* Reduces Edema
* Mimics the Lymphatic System
* Promotes Lymphatic Flow by Moving Fluid in the Proper Physiological Direction (distal to proximal)
* Stimulates Circulation to Promote Wound Healing
* Delivers Continuous Flow
* Bilateral Operation
* Lightweight. Portable. Easy to Use. Cost-Effective

# Puracol Plus AG

[Acute & Surgical Wound Dressings, ][42]
[ « View All Wound Care Products][43]

A consistent cause of a non healing wound is the MMP factory creating enzymes which inhibit healing
in otherwise healthy patients. Collagen is the most common and effective MMP controller and directs
these enzymes away from the wound bed and up into the collagen layer. While most dressings only
regulate moisture content (an Alginate drying a wet wound or a Hydrogel wetting a dry wound)
Collagen actively interferes with the MMP process.

# Collagens

[Acute & Surgical Wound Dressings, ][42]
[ « View All Wound Care Products][43]

Collagens: Stimulates new tissue development.Collagen is the most common and effective MMP
controller and directs these enzymes away from the wound bed and up into the collagen layer. While
most dressings only regulate moisture content (an Alginate drying a wet wound or a Hydrogel wetting
a dry wound) Collagen actively interferes with the MMP process.

# Bioguard Barrier Dressings

[Acute & Surgical Wound Dressings, ][42]
[ « View All Wound Care Products][43]

Derma Sciences BIOGUARD Barrier Dressings have been proven to prevent bacterial penetration and
inhibit growth within wound dressings. BIOGUARD dressings provide a barrier to bacterial penetration
and results in >5-log (99.999%) kill of a broad spectrum of microbes including antibiotic resistant
organisms. PolyDADMAC is a cationic biocide that attracts bacteria and binds with it, disrupting and
destroying the cell wall. PolyDADMAC is the active component within BIOGUARD. These dressings are
non-toxic to healthy cells. BIOGUARD has a patented manufacturing process that makes it the only
dressing that is non-leaching, non-resistant and non-toxic. It is available in 6 different forms:
Island Dressings (Adhesive border), Conforming Bandage, Gauze Sponges, Gauze Roll, Non-Adherent
Dressings, and Packing Strips. Please Contact Us for pricing and additional information.

# AIROS Medical brings together medical device veterans dedicated to advancing compression therapy
# across lymphatic, venous, and arterial care.

We develop solutions for individuals living with lymphedema, chronic venous insufficiency, and
swelling related to cancer treatment, as well as arterial conditions such as Peripheral Arterial
Disease (PAD), Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia (CLTI), and diabetic foot complications.

[ Continue Reading][32]

[Solutions Overview][Solutions Overview]

## Patient-Oriented Solutions

**Our medical technology provides solutions** for patients suffering from these conditions,
clinicians trying to treat these complications, and DME suppliers whose purpose is to provide
effective treatment inside the home.

**Our approach to product design **is to utilize high-end technology across our entire line of
devices and garments so that patients of all ages and financial backgrounds can receive proper
therapy immediately.

[Patient][Patient]

## Solutions for Patients

If you have been diagnosed with primary or secondary lymphedema, lymphedema as a result of cancer
treatment, or Chronic Venous Insufficiency (CVI), you may be prescribed a Sequential Compression
Device (SCD) to be used at home.

For individuals living with Peripheral Arterial Disease (PAD) or Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia
(CLTI), your provider may recommend an arterial intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) device to
support circulation and promote healing. This type of therapy delivers rapid, high-pressure
compression to help increase blood flow, improve walking tolerance, reduce rest pain, and assist in
wound healing — offering a non-invasive option for patients who are not candidates for surgical
intervention or who need additional support during recovery.

[Learn More][33]

[Solutions for Patients][Solutions for Patients]
[Solutions for Medical Professionals][Solutions for Medical Professionals]

## Solutions for Medical Professionals

Our team at AIROS Medical is comprised of healthcare industry veterans who have developed
relationships with physicians and clinicians in various specialties.

[Learn More][34]

[Solutions for Medical Professionals][Solutions for Medical Professionals]
[Solutions for DMEs][Solutions for DMEs]

## Solutions for DMEs

From billing experts and insurance veterans to product, sales, and marketing support, our team
prides itself on developing long-lasting, mutually-beneficial relationships with DME suppliers. Our
focus is in helping our DME partners compete and learn how to help treat patients for years to come.

[Learn More][35]

[Solutions for DMEs][Solutions for DMEs]

Are you a patient with questions about your device? A DME supplier interested in learning about
compression devices? A clinician seeking product information? Please contact us to speak with an
AIROS Medical representative.

# AIROS Medical brings together medical device veterans dedicated to advancing compression therapy
# across lymphatic, venous, and arterial care.

We develop solutions for individuals living with lymphedema, chronic venous insufficiency, and
swelling related to cancer treatment, as well as arterial conditions such as Peripheral Arterial
Disease (PAD), Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia (CLTI), and diabetic foot complications.

[ Continue Reading][32]

[Solutions Overview][Solutions Overview]

## Patient-Oriented Solutions

**Our medical technology provides solutions** for patients suffering from these conditions,
clinicians trying to treat these complications, and DME suppliers whose purpose is to provide
effective treatment inside the home.

**Our approach to product design **is to utilize high-end technology across our entire line of
devices and garments so that patients of all ages and financial backgrounds can receive proper
therapy immediately.

[Patient][Patient]

## Solutions for Patients

If you have been diagnosed with primary or secondary lymphedema, lymphedema as a result of cancer
treatment, or Chronic Venous Insufficiency (CVI), you may be prescribed a Sequential Compression
Device (SCD) to be used at home.

For individuals living with Peripheral Arterial Disease (PAD) or Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia
(CLTI), your provider may recommend an arterial intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) device to
support circulation and promote healing. This type of therapy delivers rapid, high-pressure
compression to help increase blood flow, improve walking tolerance, reduce rest pain, and assist in
wound healing — offering a non-invasive option for patients who are not candidates for surgical
intervention or who need additional support during recovery.

# Driving Compliance and Positive Patient Outcomes

Our team at AIROS Medical is comprised of healthcare industry veterans and experts who are dedicated
to helping patients live better while reducing headaches for providers.

[ Continue Reading][33]

## Developing relationships with physicians and clinicians

We have worked with vascular surgeons, podiatrists, artery and vein specialists, cardiologists,
physical therapists, lymphedema therapists, wound care professionals, and others.

We understand that when it comes to medical devices and treatment in general, patient compliance is
vital to success and outcomes. Our goal is ultimately to help patients suffering from chronic
diseases live a better quality of life.

[Solutions for Medical Professionals][Solutions for Medical Professionals]
[Solution Texture][Solution Texture]
[Solutions for Medical Professionals][Solutions for Medical Professionals]

We value our relationships with **healthcare providers** and our ability to help various types of
**physicians** and **medical personnel** treat chronic conditions.

### Conditions Treated

We specialize in designing, engineering, and manufacturing compression therapy devices that support
patients living with lymphedema, Chronic Venous Insufficiency (CVI), and other venous complications.
This includes lymphedema that many breast cancer patients must manage following surgery, radiation,
or other treatments.

In addition to our lymphatic and venous solutions, we also provide compression technology to help
support patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease (PAD) and Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia (CLTI)
who may require increased arterial blood flow to aid wound healing, reduce rest pain, or improve
mobility.

Our pneumatic compression devices, upper-body garments, lower-extremity garments, lower-truncal
garments, and arterial compression system are relied upon daily by physicians, lymphedema
therapists, vascular specialists, podiatrists, and other healthcare professionals.

We value our relationships with the providers who trust our technology to help patients manage
chronic conditions safely and effectively.

### At-Home Therapy

Our line of Sequential Compression Devices—also known as arm and leg compression pumps—is primarily
used at home to support long-term management of lymphedema and venous disorders. Once prescribed,
patients work with a DME supplier who provides the device, garments, and education needed to begin
therapy safely and confidently.

For patients with arterial insufficiency, our ARTAIRA™ arterial compression device offers an at-home
option designed to support blood flow and wound healing through high-pressure intermittent pneumatic
compression (IPC). Like our lymphatic pumps, ARTAIRA is delivered through trusted DME partners who
ensure proper setup and patient training.

We work closely with our DME network to make sure patients receive the correct therapy based on
their clinician’s prescription—whether managing lymphatic, venous, or arterial conditions.

### Intuitive Device Design

Every device in our portfolio is built with patient ease-of-use in mind. Our compression systems
feature intuitive controls, clear displays, and simple operation so patients can begin therapy with
confidence.

Clinicians and DME suppliers can easily set prescribed pressures, treatment modes, and cycle times.
Whether using one of our lymphatic pumps or the ARTAIRA arterial device, patients can begin therapy
with just a few button presses, making it easier to stay consistent with their prescribed care.

### Usage Data Feature

We also included a Usage Data feature that tracks how often patients utilize the devices. Viewing
this data can help chart or revise patient treatment plans and promote compliance.

Learn more about how our [products][34] work, including videos that provide operational tutorials.

Please [contact us][35] immediately if you have any questions about our devices, the conditions we
treat, or any other matters.

# Working to Help Patients Feel Better & Live Healthier

AIROS Medical designs, manufactures, and distributes compression pumps to help patients who are
dealing with PAD, arterial disease, primary or secondary lymphedema, chronic venous insufficiency
(CVI), and other disorders.

[ Continue Reading][33]

## Providing compression therapy treatments to help people like you feel and live better.

If you have been diagnosed with primary or secondary lymphedema, lymphedema related to cancer
treatment, Chronic Venous Insufficiency (CVI), or arterial conditions such as Peripheral Arterial
Disease (PAD) or Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia (CLTI), you may be prescribed a compression
therapy device to support your care at home.

Compression therapy can help patients experiencing swelling, venous ulcers, slow-healing wounds,
poor circulation, or discomfort related to venous or arterial insufficiency.

AIROS Medical designs, engineers, and manufactures a full portfolio of therapy solutions — including
Sequential Compression Devices (SCDs) for lymphedema and venous complications and the ARTAIRA™
Arterial Compression Device for PAD and CLTI.

For more than 20 years, our team has worked alongside podiatrists, vascular surgeons, wound care
specialists, and certified lymphedema therapists to ensure patients receive safe, effective, and
clinically supported compression therapy. Our mission is simple: help people move, heal, and live
better through proven, accessible technology.

AIROS Medical does not dispense devices directly to patients. Instead, we partner with Durable
Medical Equipment (DME) suppliers who deliver our pumps and garments, provide education, and ensure
patients receive the therapy prescribed by their clinicians.

[Solutions for Patients][Solutions for Patients]
[Solution Texture][Solution Texture]
[Patient][Patient]

We understand that when it comes to medical devices, and treatment in general, **patient compliance
is vital to success and outcomes**. Our goal is ultimately to help patients suffering from chronic
diseases **live a better quality of life**.

### Conditions Treated

Our compression therapy devices provide treatment for the following conditions:
* PAD
* Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia
* Diabetic foot ulcers
* Gangrene
* Arterial foot ulcers
* Lymphedema
* Chronic Venous Insufficiency (CVI)
* Venous Stasis Ulcers
* Other Venous Insufficiencies
* Peripheral Edema

Learn more about the specific [conditions][34] AIROS Medical specializes in treating.

### At-Home Therapy

Our suite of compression therapy devices supports both lymphatic and arterial patient
needs—providing effective home-based treatment that helps patients stay consistent with their care.

For lymphatic and venous patients, our Sequential Compression Devices (SCDs) – also known as arm and
leg compression pumps – deliver gentle, gradient pressure designed to help reduce swelling and
improve fluid movement.

For arterial patients, our ARTAIRA™ Arterial Compression Device delivers high-pressure, intermittent
pneumatic compression (IPC) designed to help increase arterial blood flow, support wound healing,
and reduce ischemic discomfort.

Once prescribed either a lymphatic or arterial device, patients are connected with a knowledgeable
DME supplier who guides them through setup and use in the comfort of their homes.

We ensure that each partner in our DME network is well-trained in compression therapy and familiar
with our full portfolio so that clinicians and patients receive the correct therapy for their
condition.

### Intuitive Device Design

Whether supporting lymphatic, venous, or arterial conditions, we design all AIROS Medical devices to
be intuitive, user-friendly, and easy to operate.

DME suppliers and healthcare professionals can quickly set the appropriate pressures, modes, and
cycle times for each device. Patients can begin therapy with just a few button presses—keeping
treatment simple, consistent, and accessible regardless of the condition being managed.

From gentle gradient compression for lymphedema and CVI, to rapid, high-pressure cycles for
improving arterial flow with ARTAIRA™, our entire portfolio was created to support life in motion
and help patients stay consistent with their therapy at home.

### Insurance

Sequential Compression Devices (SCDs) — also referred to as Pneumatic Compression Devices (PCDs) —
are commonly reimbursed by Medicare and most private insurance plans. These devices are used to help
manage lymphedema, Chronic Venous Insufficiency (CVI), and other swelling-related conditions.

For patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease (PAD) or Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia (CLTI),
arterial compression therapy may also be covered when medically necessary. Coverage varies depending
on diagnosis, clinical documentation, and insurer requirements.

Because every patient’s situation is unique, it’s important to check directly with your Medicare
plan or private insurance carrier to understand what equipment and services are included in your
benefits.

Our team at AIROS Medical has extensive experience in the DME industry. We understand both the

## Helping make DMEs competitive and successful

AIROS Medical is dedicated to providing advanced, high-quality devices and outstanding
communication, service, and support to help make DMEs competitive and successful.

From billing experts and insurance veterans to product, sales, and marketing support, our team
prides itself on developing long-lasting, mutually beneficial relationships with DME suppliers. Our
focus is on helping our DME partners compete and learn how to help treat patients for years to come.

From billing experts and insurance veterans to product, sales, and marketing support, our team
prides itself on **developing long-lasting, mutually-beneficial relationships with DME suppliers**.

### Referral Sources

The following types of healthcare professionals utilize our devices and garments.
* Podiatrists
* Wound Care Professionals
* Vascular Surgeons
* Physical Therapists
* Family/General Practice
* Orthopedic Surgeons
* Cardiologists
* Oncologists
* Lymphedema Therapists

### Products

Our goal with product design has always been to offer high-end devices and garments at an affordable
price for DMEs so that they can remain competitive and support the patients and clinicians they
serve. We have designed and manufactured various Sequential Compression Devices, drawing from
decades in the pneumatic compression space. We launched in 2018 with the AIROS 6 and the AIROS 8,
and have continued to innovate and bring new devices with more features to the market.

The [AIROS 6][34] is a 6-chamber compression pump utilized to treat lymphedema, venous
insufficiencies in the lower limbs, and other complications. The AIROS 6P operates the same way, but
adds the Peristaltic operating mode that is preferred by many lymphedema therapists for upper
extremity treatment.

The [AIROS 8][35] is an 8-chamber compression pump that has a higher reimbursement, namely because
of added features and the ability to change pressures in each garment chamber. The AIROS 8P also
features the Peristaltic Mode, and like the AIROS 6P has a larger pump and 100-240 VAC electrical
rating for use anywhere in the world.

All of our devices are used with our full line of [compression garments][36], available in dozens of
sizes and configurations. The AIROS 6P and AIROS 8P also work with our [truncal compression
garments][37], which are pants-like models that treat abdominal and pelvic swelling.

### Billing

AIROS Medical’s team includes DME industry veterans well-versed in Medicare, Medicaid, and private
insurance regulations around our various products.

We provide knowledge to our DME partners to ensure that compression pumps get billed correctly, and
that the correct paperwork gets completed.

DMEs leverage our expertise in the area of billing and insurance every day to help them be compliant
and successful.

### Support

Learn more about our [products][38], including videos providing tutorials on how our devices and
garments work.

DMEs that work with AIROS Medical receive a support packet with various resources to help them.

If you have any questions or are interested in providing AIROS Medical’s product line,
please [contact us][39] immediately.

###### Our History

### Founded on decades of experience

AIROS Medical was founded in 2016 outside of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania by medical device experts
with decades of experience in Durable Medical Equipment (DME).

Our leadership team is comprised of DME owners who had marketed and sold pneumatic compression
devices from various manufacturers for years. Their experience working with lymphedema therapists,
vascular surgeons, and other medical professionals, coupled with acquired billing and insurance
expertise, led them to consider creating their own devices.

After meeting with certified lymphedema therapists (CLTs), physical therapists, specialty
physicians, and other DME providers, the team formed AIROS Medical with the goal of engineering and
manufacturing devices and garments with the features that patients and clinicians prefer at a price
point that would allow DMEs to provide these products to as many patients as possible.

Today, medical professionals, patients, and DMEs across the United States rely on AIROS Medical’s
product line to efficiently and effectively treat lymphatic and venous disorders.

Simply put, our goals are anchored in solving problems and reducing headaches for the people we care
about: patients, caregivers, medical professionals, and our DME partners.

AIROS Medical has made our mission to help improve the quality of life for people suffering from

###### Outside In – Clinician value proposition

For Clinicians

For the clinicians treating lymphatic and venous disorders, to maintain results of in-person therapy
when the patient returns home, AIROS Medical provides a user-friendly, affordable compression
therapy device designed to increase compliance so patients can reduce swelling and pain, allowing
them to live healthier and more active lifestyles.

For Patients

For patients with lower and upper extremity lymphatic and vascular conditions with lack of mobility
and flexibility, Airos Medical provides an in-home state of the art compression device that delivers
relief from edema while providing improved circulation, mobility and skin integrity allowing for a
much-improved quality of life.

## John Evans, DPM, DABFAS, FACFAS

#### Medical Advisor

## Gerry Makoid

#### President and CEO

Gerry has been the President and CEO of AIROS Medical since its inception in 2016. Prior to
co-founding AIROS, Gerry has worked for sales teams in the Philadelphia area primarily focused on
regional territory development and sales goals in the mid-Atlantic region. Gerry finds the most joy
in his work with AIROS seeing the positive effect that our devices have on a patients’ quality of
life.

## Michael Allerton

#### VP of Sales

Michael comes to AIROS with years of experience in medical device sales, new business development,
and sales operations. He joined the team as Vice President of Sales and is excited to see how the
AIROS devices can help alleviate and manage symptoms of lymphedema and venous disorders.

## Darren Behuniak

#### Chief Operating Officer

Darren comes to AIROS with over a decade of experience in corporate marketing and start-up
environments. Throughout his career, he has helped a variety of organizations generate leads,
increase sales, and develop a strong online presence. At AIROS, he is responsible for driving
multiple FDA 510k clearances of medical technology and helping launch the company as a co-founder.

## Chris Allerton

#### VP of Business Development

Chris comes to AIROS with years of experience sourcing new business opportunities in the medical
device industry. Chris has been the VP of Business Development here at AIROS since 2018 and finds
the most reward in his work when he hears about the successes that the patients have had using our
devices to manage their symptoms.

## Adrien MacKenzie

#### Clinical Advisor

Adie MacKenzie is a national board-certified health and wellness coach and a Certified Lymphedema
Therapist. She has over 40 years of experience in manual therapy, including medical massage and
physical therapy. She currently treats lymphedema patients and people with chronic pain and chronic
illnesses as part of her private practice.

## Kelly Sturm

#### Clinical Advisor

Kelly is a physical therapist, Certified Lymphedema Therapist, and one of the first national
board-certified oncology clinical specialists in the United States. She serves as an instructor at
Concordia University’s Physical Therapy Program and a guest speaker at various conferences,
programs, and community groups. She also owns Cancer Rehab PT, LLC, an educational content company
focused on educating individuals interested in lymphedema, oncology rehabilitation, and physical
therapy.

## Betty Westbrook

#### Clinical Advisor

Betty Westbrook is a Physical Therapist Assistant certified in advanced lymphedema management.
Through her passion to educate others about Lymphedema she created Lymphedema Podcast, and this
introduced her to many more opportunities to advocate for the underserved Lymphedema community. In
2019 Betty created the first summer camp for children with Lymphedema in the United States. Camp
Watchme is a time for children with Lymphedema and their parents to immerse themselves in a
community of others who understand exactly what they are going through. Advocacy, education, and
community are three things Betty values most as a voice for the Lymphedema community.

## John Evans, DPM, DABFAS, FACFAS

#### Medical Advisor

Dr. Evans received his DPM from the Temple University College of Podiatric Medicine and has a BS in
Pharmacy from the University of Connecticut. He is board-certified by the American Board of Foot and
Ankle Surgery (Foot and Ankle) and is Chief of Podiatry at Corewell Health (Beaumont) Medical Center
in Dearborn, Michigan.

He has served as Chair of the American Podiatric Medical Association (APMA) Health Policy and
Practice Committee and as a Medicare Carrier Advisory Committee (CAC) representative for over 20
years and was the 2018 recipient of the APMA Award of Excellence. He served as the Podiatric
representative to the PAD Guidelines Writing Committee of the American Heart Assn. and American
College of Cardiology which were published in 2024 and serves as the Podiatric representative of
APMA to the AHA PVD Leadership Council. He is active with the American Board of Foot and Ankle
Surgery, having served on multiple committees including their Board of Directors for eight years,
and is the immediate Past-Chair of their Communications Committee. He is active with the American
Limb Preservation Society on the Health Equity and Advocacy Committee as Co-Chair of the Research
and Data Analysis Sub-Committee, the CLI Global Society, and as faculty for the New Cardiovascular
Horizons organization, Desert Foot, and Goldfarb Foundation.

Dr. Evans is a nationally recognized speaker on a variety of topics including Peripheral Arterial
Disease, the Diabetic Foot, Limb Salvage and Preservation, Physician Burnout, Dealing with the
Difficult Patient, and Mindfulness in Medicine. Dr. Evans is in private practice in southeast
Michigan.

# AIROS Medical brings together medical device veterans dedicated to advancing compression therapy
# across lymphatic, venous, and arterial care.

We develop solutions for individuals living with lymphedema, chronic venous insufficiency, and
swelling related to cancer treatment, as well as arterial conditions such as Peripheral Arterial
Disease (PAD), Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia (CLTI), and diabetic foot complications.

[ Continue Reading][32]

[Solutions Overview][Solutions Overview]

## Patient-Oriented Solutions

**Our medical technology provides solutions** for patients suffering from these conditions,
clinicians trying to treat these complications, and DME suppliers whose purpose is to provide
effective treatment inside the home.

**Our approach to product design **is to utilize high-end technology across our entire line of
devices and garments so that patients of all ages and financial backgrounds can receive proper
therapy immediately.

[Patient][Patient]

## Solutions for Patients

If you have been diagnosed with primary or secondary lymphedema, lymphedema as a result of cancer
treatment, or Chronic Venous Insufficiency (CVI), you may be prescribed a Sequential Compression
Device (SCD) to be used at home.

For individuals living with Peripheral Arterial Disease (PAD) or Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia
(CLTI), your provider may recommend an arterial intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) device to
support circulation and promote healing. This type of therapy delivers rapid, high-pressure
compression to help increase blood flow, improve walking tolerance, reduce rest pain, and assist in
wound healing — offering a non-invasive option for patients who are not candidates for surgical
intervention or who need additional support during recovery.

# Working to Help Patients Feel Better & Live Healthier

AIROS Medical designs, manufactures, and distributes compression pumps to help patients who are
dealing with PAD, arterial disease, primary or secondary lymphedema, chronic venous insufficiency
(CVI), and other disorders.

[ Continue Reading][33]

## Providing compression therapy treatments to help people like you feel and live better.

If you have been diagnosed with primary or secondary lymphedema, lymphedema related to cancer
treatment, Chronic Venous Insufficiency (CVI), or arterial conditions such as Peripheral Arterial
Disease (PAD) or Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia (CLTI), you may be prescribed a compression
therapy device to support your care at home.

Compression therapy can help patients experiencing swelling, venous ulcers, slow-healing wounds,
poor circulation, or discomfort related to venous or arterial insufficiency.

AIROS Medical designs, engineers, and manufactures a full portfolio of therapy solutions — including
Sequential Compression Devices (SCDs) for lymphedema and venous complications and the ARTAIRA™
Arterial Compression Device for PAD and CLTI.

For more than 20 years, our team has worked alongside podiatrists, vascular surgeons, wound care
specialists, and certified lymphedema therapists to ensure patients receive safe, effective, and
clinically supported compression therapy. Our mission is simple: help people move, heal, and live
better through proven, accessible technology.

AIROS Medical does not dispense devices directly to patients. Instead, we partner with Durable
Medical Equipment (DME) suppliers who deliver our pumps and garments, provide education, and ensure
patients receive the therapy prescribed by their clinicians.

[Solutions for Patients][Solutions for Patients]
[Solution Texture][Solution Texture]
[Patient][Patient]

We understand that when it comes to medical devices, and treatment in general, **patient compliance
is vital to success and outcomes**. Our goal is ultimately to help patients suffering from chronic
diseases **live a better quality of life**.

### Conditions Treated

Our compression therapy devices provide treatment for the following conditions:
* PAD
* Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia
* Diabetic foot ulcers
* Gangrene
* Arterial foot ulcers
* Lymphedema
* Chronic Venous Insufficiency (CVI)
* Venous Stasis Ulcers
* Other Venous Insufficiencies
* Peripheral Edema

Learn more about the specific [conditions][34] AIROS Medical specializes in treating.

### At-Home Therapy

Our suite of compression therapy devices supports both lymphatic and arterial patient
needs—providing effective home-based treatment that helps patients stay consistent with their care.

For lymphatic and venous patients, our Sequential Compression Devices (SCDs) – also known as arm and
leg compression pumps – deliver gentle, gradient pressure designed to help reduce swelling and
improve fluid movement.

For arterial patients, our ARTAIRA™ Arterial Compression Device delivers high-pressure, intermittent
pneumatic compression (IPC) designed to help increase arterial blood flow, support wound healing,
and reduce ischemic discomfort.

Once prescribed either a lymphatic or arterial device, patients are connected with a knowledgeable
DME supplier who guides them through setup and use in the comfort of their homes.

We ensure that each partner in our DME network is well-trained in compression therapy and familiar
with our full portfolio so that clinicians and patients receive the correct therapy for their
condition.

### Intuitive Device Design

Whether supporting lymphatic, venous, or arterial conditions, we design all AIROS Medical devices to
be intuitive, user-friendly, and easy to operate.

DME suppliers and healthcare professionals can quickly set the appropriate pressures, modes, and
cycle times for each device. Patients can begin therapy with just a few button presses—keeping
treatment simple, consistent, and accessible regardless of the condition being managed.

From gentle gradient compression for lymphedema and CVI, to rapid, high-pressure cycles for
improving arterial flow with ARTAIRA™, our entire portfolio was created to support life in motion
and help patients stay consistent with their therapy at home.

### Insurance

Sequential Compression Devices (SCDs) — also referred to as Pneumatic Compression Devices (PCDs) —
are commonly reimbursed by Medicare and most private insurance plans. These devices are used to help
manage lymphedema, Chronic Venous Insufficiency (CVI), and other swelling-related conditions.

For patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease (PAD) or Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia (CLTI),
arterial compression therapy may also be covered when medically necessary. Coverage varies depending
on diagnosis, clinical documentation, and insurer requirements.

Because every patient’s situation is unique, it’s important to check directly with your Medicare
plan or private insurance carrier to understand what equipment and services are included in your
benefits.

### Products

Our goal with product design has always been to offer high-end devices and garments at an affordable
price for DMEs so that they can remain competitive and support the patients and clinicians they
serve. We have designed and manufactured various Sequential Compression Devices, drawing from
decades in the pneumatic compression space. We launched in 2018 with the AIROS 6 and the AIROS 8,
and have continued to innovate and bring new devices with more features to the market.

The [AIROS 6][34] is a 6-chamber compression pump utilized to treat lymphedema, venous
insufficiencies in the lower limbs, and other complications. The AIROS 6P operates the same way, but
adds the Peristaltic operating mode that is preferred by many lymphedema therapists for upper
extremity treatment.

The [AIROS 8][35] is an 8-chamber compression pump that has a higher reimbursement, namely because
of added features and the ability to change pressures in each garment chamber. The AIROS 8P also
features the Peristaltic Mode, and like the AIROS 6P has a larger pump and 100-240 VAC electrical
rating for use anywhere in the world.

All of our devices are used with our full line of [compression garments][36], available in dozens of
sizes and configurations. The AIROS 6P and AIROS 8P also work with our [truncal compression
garments][37], which are pants-like models that treat abdominal and pelvic swelling.

### Billing

AIROS Medical’s team includes DME industry veterans well-versed in Medicare, Medicaid, and private
insurance regulations around our various products.

We provide knowledge to our DME partners to ensure that compression pumps get billed correctly, and
that the correct paperwork gets completed.

DMEs leverage our expertise in the area of billing and insurance every day to help them be compliant
and successful.

## John Evans, DPM, DABFAS, FACFAS

#### Medical Advisor

## Gerry Makoid

#### President and CEO

Gerry has been the President and CEO of AIROS Medical since its inception in 2016. Prior to
co-founding AIROS, Gerry has worked for sales teams in the Philadelphia area primarily focused on
regional territory development and sales goals in the mid-Atlantic region. Gerry finds the most joy
in his work with AIROS seeing the positive effect that our devices have on a patients’ quality of
life.

## Michael Allerton

#### VP of Sales

Michael comes to AIROS with years of experience in medical device sales, new business development,
and sales operations. He joined the team as Vice President of Sales and is excited to see how the
AIROS devices can help alleviate and manage symptoms of lymphedema and venous disorders.

## Darren Behuniak

#### Chief Operating Officer

Darren comes to AIROS with over a decade of experience in corporate marketing and start-up
environments. Throughout his career, he has helped a variety of organizations generate leads,
increase sales, and develop a strong online presence. At AIROS, he is responsible for driving
multiple FDA 510k clearances of medical technology and helping launch the company as a co-founder.

## Chris Allerton

#### VP of Business Development

Chris comes to AIROS with years of experience sourcing new business opportunities in the medical
device industry. Chris has been the VP of Business Development here at AIROS since 2018 and finds
the most reward in his work when he hears about the successes that the patients have had using our
devices to manage their symptoms.

## Adrien MacKenzie

#### Clinical Advisor

Adie MacKenzie is a national board-certified health and wellness coach and a Certified Lymphedema
Therapist. She has over 40 years of experience in manual therapy, including medical massage and
physical therapy. She currently treats lymphedema patients and people with chronic pain and chronic
illnesses as part of her private practice.

## Kelly Sturm

#### Clinical Advisor

Kelly is a physical therapist, Certified Lymphedema Therapist, and one of the first national
board-certified oncology clinical specialists in the United States. She serves as an instructor at
Concordia University’s Physical Therapy Program and a guest speaker at various conferences,
programs, and community groups. She also owns Cancer Rehab PT, LLC, an educational content company
focused on educating individuals interested in lymphedema, oncology rehabilitation, and physical
therapy.

## Betty Westbrook

#### Clinical Advisor

Betty Westbrook is a Physical Therapist Assistant certified in advanced lymphedema management.
Through her passion to educate others about Lymphedema she created Lymphedema Podcast, and this
introduced her to many more opportunities to advocate for the underserved Lymphedema community. In
2019 Betty created the first summer camp for children with Lymphedema in the United States. Camp
Watchme is a time for children with Lymphedema and their parents to immerse themselves in a
community of others who understand exactly what they are going through. Advocacy, education, and
community are three things Betty values most as a voice for the Lymphedema community.

## John Evans, DPM, DABFAS, FACFAS

#### Medical Advisor

Dr. Evans received his DPM from the Temple University College of Podiatric Medicine and has a BS in
Pharmacy from the University of Connecticut. He is board-certified by the American Board of Foot and
Ankle Surgery (Foot and Ankle) and is Chief of Podiatry at Corewell Health (Beaumont) Medical Center
in Dearborn, Michigan.

He has served as Chair of the American Podiatric Medical Association (APMA) Health Policy and
Practice Committee and as a Medicare Carrier Advisory Committee (CAC) representative for over 20
years and was the 2018 recipient of the APMA Award of Excellence. He served as the Podiatric
representative to the PAD Guidelines Writing Committee of the American Heart Assn. and American
College of Cardiology which were published in 2024 and serves as the Podiatric representative of
APMA to the AHA PVD Leadership Council. He is active with the American Board of Foot and Ankle
Surgery, having served on multiple committees including their Board of Directors for eight years,
and is the immediate Past-Chair of their Communications Committee. He is active with the American
Limb Preservation Society on the Health Equity and Advocacy Committee as Co-Chair of the Research
and Data Analysis Sub-Committee, the CLI Global Society, and as faculty for the New Cardiovascular
Horizons organization, Desert Foot, and Goldfarb Foundation.

Dr. Evans is a nationally recognized speaker on a variety of topics including Peripheral Arterial
Disease, the Diabetic Foot, Limb Salvage and Preservation, Physician Burnout, Dealing with the
Difficult Patient, and Mindfulness in Medicine. Dr. Evans is in private practice in southeast
Michigan.

**Aims and Scope**
*Annals of Phlebology (Ann Phlebology)* is a peer-reviewed journal which publishes scientific
articles regarding all aspects of venous pathology, including clinical practice, experimental and
applied research, and education. The ANN PHLEBOLOGY is the official journal of the Korean Society
for Phlebology (KSP) and is published bi-annually on the last days of June and December. The ANN
PHLEBOLOGY aims to promote active communication among not only members of the Korean Society for
Phlebology but also to the various professionals with interest in venous pathology. To achieve this,
we publish original articles, review articles, brief communications including case reports, letters
to the editor, and commentaries or opinion on the topics of importance to venous pathology.

all_classified.polished_summary: Annphlebology is a specialized publication focused on the field of phlebology, offering valuable insights into venous diseases and treatments. The journal publishes research articles, reviews, and clinical trials, aiming to advance knowledge and practice in the management of chronic venous conditions. Its target audience includes medical professionals, researchers, and practitioners in the field of vascular medicine.

all_classified.company_summary: Apollo Hospitals is a leading healthcare provider in India, renowned for its comprehensive range of medical services, including advanced clinical care, research, and education. With a commitment to quality and innovation, the organization operates numerous hospitals and specialty centers across the country, catering to diverse patient needs and enhancing healthcare accessibility. Apollo Hospitals also emphasizes corporate social responsibility and sustainability, reflecting its dedication to community health and well-being.

methods of assessment¹. The most essential transfers take place multiple times throughout the daily
journey.

[Flowtron ACS900 (10)]

### VTE Prevention

 

Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a serious condition that causes death and disability worldwide, with
10 million cases each year. In order to safeguard the well-being of at-risk patients, comprehensive
prevention strategies that take into account individual clinical needs are essential.

 


[Learn more ][149]
[Natasa and Irma outside Benevit facility (23)]

### ''Movement provides a better quality of life for our residents''

For Benevit’s nursing homes, long-term sick leave time has dropped massively, partly due to
ergonomics training and use of aids. One key differentiator: the integration of the Arjo MOVE
program, which has shown positive impacts on physical and mental stress within the nursing teams,
and a better quality of life for residents.

prevention strategies that take into account individual clinical needs are essential.

 


[Learn more ][149]
[Natasa and Irma outside Benevit facility (23)]

### ''Movement provides a better quality of life for our residents''

For Benevit’s nursing homes, long-term sick leave time has dropped massively, partly due to
ergonomics training and use of aids. One key differentiator: the integration of the Arjo MOVE
program, which has shown positive impacts on physical and mental stress within the nursing teams,
and a better quality of life for residents.

[See their story here][150]
[Hygiene Relaxing (2)]

### Hygiene and Wellness

Hygiene is an essential part of well-being. Arjo integrated Hygiene and Wellness Solutions enable
you to deliver a tailored and therapeutic experience for dependent residents and patients, helping
you improve wellbeing and efficiency in your care environment.

[Explore ][151]
[MyArjo image 1]

### Introducing MyArjo: Your portal to Arjo tools and services

MyArjo is a personalised web portal providing access to Arjo tools and services with one secure
login.

Sign up to get MyArjo access and begin your journey to Empower Movement today.

[Discover MyArjo][152]
[Academy banner 1920x450px final2.jpg]

## [ Arjo Academy: Your path to professional development ][153]

Access a comprehensive range of accredited and non-accredited live and

on-demand webinars, courses and E-Learnings.

 

 

START YOUR LEARNING JOURNEY
[Arjo blue studio background]

## Our Product Categories

##### [Patient Handling][154]

For patients and residents with limited or impaired mobility, time spent out of bed may be a
specific rehabilitation goal or the highlight of their day.

##### [Medical beds][155]

We offer a wide range of hospital and long term healthcare beds that allow good infection control,
offer enhanced ergonomics, comfort, safety and ease of use, and promote effective risk management.

##### [Hygiene][156]

Our hygiene solutions are designed to facilitate efficient and secure hygiene care and wellness
routines while helping to reduce workload for caregivers.

##### [Pressure Injury Prevention][157]

Arjo empowers you with the ability to elevate the pressure injury prevention pathway in your care
environment, equipping you with the knowledge, skills and tools to act on a new standard of clinical
excellence and deliver measurable outcomes in early identification, prevention and management of
pressure injuries..

##### [Disinfection][158]

Flusher disinfectors and flusher liquids to support your infection control strategy.

##### [VTE prevention][159]

While healthcare facilities are aware of the risk of VTE, care providers do not always have the
time, training or resources to implement optimal prevention strategies. With the Arjo Flowtron
Active Compression System, professional caregivers can deliver safe, convenient and flexible VTE
prevention therapy that helps them achieve compliance and optimal clinical efficacy.

[Positive 8 ]

### The Positive Eight Philosophy

Our care philosophy explains how facilitating mobility can catalyse a chain of benefits impacting
quality of life, caregiver satisfaction, operational efficiency, and financial outcomes. 

[read more ][160]
[Mobility gallery Long Term Care Group]

### Mobility gallery

Based on 5 levels of mobility from A to E, the Arjo Mobility Gallery provides a basis for
understanding how an individual can contribute to their mobility, as well as how to safeguard
caregivers from injuries.

[read more][161]
[Sara Flex with Sara 3000 Standing Sling (5)]

### Arjo MOVE

Rooted in clinical evidence and driven by your facility data, Arjo MOVE programs arm you with the
tools and knowledge to reach your clinical and operational goals.

[read more ][162]

# Welcome to Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals

#### Hospital Numbers

If you need to contact a department or ward then please call our main switchboard:

**01784 884488** (Ashford Hospital)
**01932 872000** (St Peter's Hospital)

If you have an impairment or sensory loss and have specific communication needs please let our
operator know.

If you are using a [textphone][205],
prefix all numbers with **18001**.


#### Our CQC Rating

[[Find out more about out CQC rating by clicking here]][206]

#### We are very proud of our hospitals and our staff, and aim to provide a high quality service for
#### our patients at all times.

We shall do our best to make your visit as comfortable as possible and our staff will do all they
can to assist you.

If you want to find out more about the Trust and our hospitals, please visit our [About Us][207]
section.

We welcome any [comments or feedback][208] you would like to share with us. Listening to our
patients helps us to get things right.

## Resources for Patients and Visitors

#### [Choose Well][252]

Our A&E department is currently very busy and** is for urgent and emergency care only**. **Think
before you visit**, consider alternative services with shorter wait times.

For helpful information on non-emergency services, see information above, or call NHS 111 or visit
[111.nhs.uk][253]

Read more about [finding the right services][254] in our area.

#### [Book your Blood Test][255]

Ashford and St Peter’s Hospitals have introduced an [online booking option for blood tests][256],
giving patients the ability to book in advance at a time that is convenient to them.

This helps reduce waiting times and minimise delays for patients.

A phlebotomy (blood test) service is provided on the Ashford Hospital site only.

#### [Travelling to the Trust][257]

We have details about [travelling to our hospitals][258], [parking][259], and [site maps][260].
* [Ashford Hospital][261]
* [St Peter's Hospital][262]

Do take care travelling in bad weather conditions:
* [Met Office Website][263]
* [Traffic England Website][264]

 

[[Managing Respiratory Viruses]][265]

#### [Visiting Update][266]

For details about times please see our [visiting section][267] including exceptions for some wards.

#### [Advice for Visitors][268]

We recognise that visiting a person in hospital plays a vital part in aiding their recovery. We
encourage visitors to take part in social interaction with patients and to share in their care where
appropriate. Please respect other patients when visiting and keep noise to a minimum. We therefore
ask that no more than two people visit a patient at any one time.

#### Visiting Measures

We ask everyone to follow these basic infection prevention and control measures in our hospitals:
* Do not visit the hospital if you have the following symptoms:
  
  * New onset cough or an ongoing cough that is not improving
  * Raised temperature
  * Diarrhoea and / or vomiting
     
* If you do have these symptoms and visiting is essential, and cannot be delayed for a few days
  whilst you recover, e.g. the patient is very unwell / dying, then please telephone the ward
  concerned and ask to speak to the nurse-in-charge.
  
  We are always keen to support visiting in these situations.
* Practice good respiratory hygiene: cover your nose and mouth when coughing or sneezing using a
  tissue or the inside of your elbow. Dispose of tissues immediately following use and clean your
  hands.
* Clean your hands on entering and leaving our clinical areas, e.g. wards, using the hand wash
  basins or alcohol hand sanitiser available inside each patient multi-bed bay and single rooms.
* Visitors are not routinely required to wear disposable gloves and plastic aprons; but should be
  worn if you are helping the patient with their personal hygiene care.

## Putting Patients First

[[Emergency Department - Find out more about our Emergency Department]][269]

#### [Emergencies][270]

Our [emergency department][271] is located at St Peter’s Hospital. Please only visit us if you are
seriously ill or it is an emergency. Minor injuries will be directed to our [Urgent Treatment
Centre][272] opposite A&E. We also have a new [Urgent Care Centre][273].

Through its strategic focus on health and community well-being, Ashfordstpeters aims to enhance the overall healthcare experience for its diverse patient population.

# BMJ Open

is an online, open access journal, dedicated to publishing medical research from all disciplines and
therapeutic areas.

**Impact Factor:** 2.5
**Citescore:** 4.1
[All metrics >>][39]

The journal publishes all research study types, from protocols through phase I trials to
meta-analyses, including small, specialist studies, and negative studies. Publishing procedures are
built around fully open peer review and continuous publication, publishing research online as soon
as the article is ready.

*BMJ Open* aims to promote transparency in the publication process by publishing reviewer reports
and previous versions of manuscripts as pre-publication histories. Authors are asked to pay
article-publishing charges on acceptance; the ability to pay does not influence editorial decisions.

All papers are included in MEDLINE/PubMed and Science Citation Index Expanded (Web of Science).

[Current Issue][40][[Journal Current Issue]][41]

BMJ Open accepts submissions on a range of article types, including original research, cohort
profiles and protocols.

The Author Information section provides specific article requirements to help you turn your research
into an article suitable for BMJ Open.

Information is also provided on [editorial policies][42] and [open access][43].

# About Us

### Redefining What’s Possible

#### We are a late-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing novel therapies for life-threatening
#### immune and thrombotic conditions.

We are a late-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing novel therapies for life-threatening immune
and thrombotic conditions. Our lead program, CAD-1005, is a first-in-class 12-LOX inhibitor for the
treatment of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT), a deadly immune-mediated thrombotic disorder.
Our broader pipeline includes tecarfarin, a Phase 3-ready oral vitamin K antagonist for the
treatment of patients with end-stage kidney disease and those with left ventricular assist devices,
and frunexian, a parenteral, clinical-stage Factor XIa inhibitor designed for use in acute hospital
settings.

[ See Pipeline ][56]

### Dedicated Leadership

Our mission is supported by a dedicated leadership team, board of directors, and experienced
scientific advisors with extensive knowledge in cardiology, drug development, manufacturing, and
commercialization.

### Management Team

Loading...

###### Quang Pham

Chairman & Chief Executive Officer

[ Read Bio ][57]

###### Quang Pham

Chairman & Chief Executive Officer

Quang Pham has served as our Chief Executive Officer since he formed the Company. He previously
served as Chairman & CEO of Espero BioPharma, Inc., a company he also founded and the previous
sponsor of the tecarfarin IND. He then served as a consultant to HESP LLC, the assignee for Espero
to Horizon Technology Finance. Previously, Mr. Pham was a partner with D+R LATHIAN, LLC, a life
sciences multichannel marketing agency. Prior to joining D+R LATHIAN, he founded and served as
Chairman and CEO of Lathian Systems, Inc., a digital and database marketing company serving the
pharmaceutical industry until 2012 when the company was acquired by D&R Communications, LLC. He has
a Bachelor of Arts in Economics from UCLA, and served as a U.S. Marine Corps Officer. We believe Mr.
Pham is qualified to serve on our Board of Directors because of his significant business, mergers
and acquisitions, and fundraising experience, numerous interactions with the FDA, continuous
six-year history with tecarfarin development, and his extensive knowledge of the pharmaceutical
industry and our competitors.

###### Jeff Cole

Chief Operating Officer

[ Read Bio ][58]

###### Jeff Cole

Chief Operating Officer

Jeff Cole has served as our Chief Operating Officer since February 2024 and brings over 25 years of
experience in global pharmaceutical manufacturing, commercial operations, finance, and corporate
development. Prior to that, Mr. Cole provided operational and financial advisory services to the
Company in his capacity as Principal of J. Scott Capital, a firm he founded to assist launch, build,
and run life science organizations. Mr. Cole also co-founded Espero BioPharma where he served as
Director, President and CFO and led multiple product acquisitions, product launches, financings, and
strategic transactions. Prior to that, Mr. Cole served as President and co-founder of MarcasUSA, a
marketer and distributor of OTC pharmaceuticals. Mr. Cole also served as CFO of Legacy
Pharmaceuticals International, a global contract manufacturing organization, and founding President
of its generic drug subsidiary, Solco Healthcare U.S. Earlier in his career, Mr. Cole held various
executive positions at Bausch Health Companies (formerly Valeant Pharmaceuticals International),
including General Manager, VP Corporate Development, and CFO North America. Prior to the
pharmaceutical industry, he worked at PwC Consulting and Deloitte. Mr. Cole holds an MBA with honors
from the University of Michigan and a BS in accounting from the University of Southern California.

###### James Ferguson, M.D., FACC, FAHA

Chief Medical Officer

James Ferguson is a distinguished medical expert with over 25 years of leadership in the
cardiovascular field and deep expertise in clinical development. Dr. Ferguson joined Cadrenal in
February 2025 from Matinas BioPharma where he served as Chief Medical Officer. Previously, Dr.
Ferguson served as Head of U.S. Cardiovascular Medical Affairs at Amgen and held several senior
positions at AstraZeneca, including Vice President of US Cardiovascular Medical and Scientific
External Relations, Therapeutic Area Vice President of Cardiovascular Global Medical Affairs, US
Development brand leader for BRILINTA, and Senior Director, Clinical Research. Before joining
AstraZeneca, he was Vice President of Surgical and Critical Care for The Medicines Company. Prior to
joining industry in 2008, he had more than 20 years of academic experience as the Associate Director
of Clinical Cardiology Research at the Texas Heart Institute, Co-Director of the Cardiology
Fellowship Training Program at St. Luke's Episcopal Hospital in Houston, where he was an Associate
Professor of Medicine at Baylor College of Medicine, and a Clinical Assistant Professor at the
University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston. Dr. Ferguson has served on the Editorial Board
of numerous peer-reviewed journals and has over 400 publications and book chapters. Dr. Ferguson
received his B.A. in Biology from Harvard College, his M.D. from the University of Pennsylvania
School of Medicine and completed his post-graduate training at the University of Michigan Medical
Center, Ann Arbor, Michigan and Beth Israel Hospital, Boston, Massachusetts.

###### Matthew Boxer, Ph.D., MBA

EVP Corporate Development

Matthew Boxer has more than 18 years of experience in drug discovery and brings deep expertise in

corporate strategy, governance, finance, and operations. Before founding Veralox, Dr. Boxer was a

Chemistry from the University of Chicago, where he received multiple awards for research and
teaching. Following completion of his Ph.D., he undertook an NIH postdoctoral fellowship and later
earned an MBA from the Johns Hopkins Carey School of Business.

strategy and fundraising. He also served as Co-Head of Translational Medicine at Inspyr Therapeutics
where he led asset acquisition and development efforts. From 2010 to 2017, Dr. Boxer was a Group
Leader at the National Institutes of Health (NIH), where he managed interdisciplinary teams spanning
biotechnology, academia, and government. Over the course of his career, Dr. Boxer has led numerous
drug discovery programs, with a particular focus on rare diseases with significant unmet clinical
needs. Dr. Boxer earned a Bachelor of Science from the University of Vermont and a Ph.D. in
Chemistry from the University of Chicago, where he received multiple awards for research and
teaching. Following completion of his Ph.D., he undertook an NIH postdoctoral fellowship and later
earned an MBA from the Johns Hopkins Carey School of Business.

all_classified.polished_summary: Cadrenal is a late-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to advancing innovative therapies for life-threatening immune and thrombotic conditions. Its core products include CAD-1005, a first-in-class 12-LOX inhibitor for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, Tecarfarin, an oral vitamin K antagonist for patients with end-stage kidney disease and left ventricular assist devices, and Frunexian, a clinical-stage Factor XIa inhibitor intended for acute hospital settings. The company focuses on improving outcomes for patients in critical healthcare scenarios, particularly those affected by severe thrombotic disorders.

With a focus on enhancing clinical research and operational efficiency, Clinical Trials Arena serves as a vital resource for stakeholders seeking to navigate the complexities of clinical development and innovation.

# About Us

**The trusted source for healthcare information and CONTINUING EDUCATION.**

Clinician.com, part of Relias, provides medical information, publications and continuing education
to healthcare professionals with the ultimate goal of improving patient care and outcomes. Formerly
known as AHC Media, Clinician.com has a long history of fostering professional development through
award-winning healthcare and clinically relevant content in emergency medicine, clinical medicine
and hospital management.

In addition to its educational publications, Clinician.com publishes special reports and study
guides on a variety of healthcare topics, most offering continuing medical education (CME) and/or
continuing education (CE).

Over the last several decades, Clinician.com has won many awards for excellence in publishing by the
National Press Club, The Society of Professional Journalists, the Jesse H. Neal Awards, the Digital
Health Awards, and other organizations.

[freeCME.com®][3], a division of Clinician.com, provides current continuing education activities
with credits at no charge to thousands of its members each month on a wide range of medical topics.

If you have any questions, please [contact us][4].

## Our Offerings

Clinician.com has a five-decade commitment to continuing education for physicians, nurses, and
allied healthcare professionals.

*For physicians*, Clinician.com is an accredited provider of *AMA PRA Category 1 Credits™* through
the Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education. We offer Continuing Medical Education
across 12 clinical and healthcare-related specialties. Clinician.com is in the top 7% of
ACCME-accredited providers for Number of Hours of Instruction and in the Number of Physicians
Reached.

*For nurses*, Clinician.com has been an accredited provider of Contact Hours through the American
Nurses Credentialing Center since 1988.

Clinician.com is also an accredited provider of continuing education credits through the American
College of Emergency Physicians, the American Academy of Pediatrics, and the American Board of
Internal Medicine.

## Awards

Since 2010, Clinician.com has earned a number of awards for our high-quality newsletters, blogs,
reporting, news coverage, and content.

View [all of our awards here][5].

# About me

### Share this post:

[ Share on X (Twitter)][10][ Share on Facebook][11][ Share on LinkedIn][12][ Share on Email][13]

## About Me

**Welcome to Doc’s Opinion.**
My name is **Axel F. Sigurdsson, MD, PhD, FACC**, and I’m the writer and editor of this blog.

I’m a practicing cardiologist in Reykjavík, Iceland, with a deep commitment to making medical
science more accessible—bridging the gap between complex research and practical understanding.

> **I write to bridge the distance between medical science and everyday life—because good medicine
> should be understood, not just practiced.**

## Clinical Background

I practice cardiology at the **Reykjavík Heart Center (Hjartamiðstöðin)**, a private heart clinic in
the Reykjavík area, and at **Myndgreining Hjartaverndar** (*The Imaging Center of the Icelandic
Heart Association*), where I specialize in interpreting **cardiovascular and coronary CT scans**.

I am a **Fellow of the American College of Cardiology (FACC)** and a member of both the **Icelandic
Society of Cardiology** and the **Swedish Society of Cardiology**. I also served as **President of
the Icelandic Cardiac Society**.

In addition to cardiology, I’m a licensed **Aviation Medical Examiner**, and I served as **Medical
Director for Icelandair** from 2004 to 2019.

## Education and Training

I earned my medical degree from the **University of Iceland** in 1984 and moved to **Sweden** for
postgraduate training in **internal medicine and cardiology** at **Sahlgrenska/Östra University
Hospital in Gothenburg**.

In **1993**, I completed my **PhD in Clinical Physiology** at the **University of Gothenburg**. My
thesis focused on:

> *“Neurohormonal Activation in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction or Chronic Congestive
> Heart Failure – With Special Reference to Treatment with ACE Inhibitors.”*

From 1995 to 1996, I completed a **clinical fellowship in interventional cardiology** at the **Royal
Jubilee Hospital** in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada.

Over the course of my career, I’ve authored and co-authored more than **100 scientific articles,
abstracts, and book chapters** in international journals and textbooks.

## About the Blog: Doc’s Opinion

I launched *Doc’s Opinion* in the spring of **2012** to offer thoughtful, evidence-based commentary
on **cardiovascular health**, **lifestyle medicine**, and **clinical science**. The blog is grounded
in the principles of **evidence-based medicine**, but it’s also shaped by curiosity, skepticism, and
a desire to connect medical knowledge with real life.

While the core focus includes:
* **Cardiovascular disease** and prevention
* **Lipidology** and cholesterol metabolism
* **Healthy lifestyle**, nutrition, and risk reduction
* **Patient education** and clinical insight

—I also write across disciplines. Many articles explore the wider **cultural, historical, and
psychological dimensions** of medicine: how guidelines are formed, how industry shapes science, how
wellness trends affect behavior, and how we think about health in the context of time, power, and
mortality. Some essays are reflective and personal. Others are investigative, analytical, or
narrative-driven. My aim is to challenge assumptions, clarify confusion, and bring depth to the
conversation around health.

A special feature of the blog is *The Heart of Power*—a historical series exploring the medical
lives of U.S. presidents. Blending biography with clinical insight, these stories examine how
illness shaped leadership, how health was concealed or weaponized, and how medicine and politics
have long been entangled in the highest office. It’s a lens on history through the pulse of power.

> **I write for both health professionals and curious readers—bridging the space between scientific
> literature and human experience.**

**Informative. Trustworthy. Accessible.**
That’s what I strive for in every post.

## Medical Disclaimer

This blog is for general informational purposes only. It does **not constitute medical advice,
diagnosis, or treatment**, nor does it create a doctor–patient relationship.
Always consult your physician or qualified healthcare provider with any medical concerns. Use of
this website and its content is at your own risk.

I was born in Vestmannaeyjar, a volcanic island close to the south coast of Iceland, on August 21,
1959.

## A List of Some of My Published Scientific Papers

[Relationship of C-reactive protein reduction to cardiovascular event reduction following treatment
with canakinumab: A secondary analysis from the CANTOS randomised controlled trial][15]

[Effect of interleukin-1β inhibition with canakinumab on incident lung cancer in patients with
atherosclerosis: Exploratory results from a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial][16]

[The cardiovascular risk reduction benefits of a low-carbohydrate diet outweigh the potential
increase in LDL-cholesterol][17]

[Outcome of myocardial revascularisation in patients fifty years old and younger.][18]

[Angiotensin Receptor Neprilysin Inhibition Compared With Enalapril on the Risk of Clinical
Progression in Surviving Patients With Heart Failure.][19]

[Benefits of Statins in Healthy Elderly Subjects What Is the Number Needed to Treat?][20]

[Comparison of 30-Day and 5-Year Outcomes of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Versus Coronary
Artery Bypass Grafting in Patients Aged how come? Well, even in the developing world, medication is becoming more
and more available – and the total risk is nearly always a sum of several issues on population
level. This really smells the same ol’ BS as the “French paradox”, doesn’t it?

3) When talking about cholesterol, Grimes makes the same moronic mistakes as cholesterol
denialists (is he one, by the way?? Axel, do you know??). E.g. citing Framingham, Grimes
argues that high plasma cholesterol levels are detrimental in only young men. Epic fail! The
very paper which Grimes cites points out that the connection between increasing overall
mortality & falling cholesterol levels in people over 50 is likely to be due to confounding
factor of disease which – besides causing untimely death – also cause cholesterol levels to
drop. Later on this has been confirmed by both extensive observational evidence and e.g.
statin trials where lowering cholesterol has been beneficial in population older than 50
years, as well. See e.g. this

[https://qjmed.oxfordjournals.org/content/94/9/457.full][63]

Not to mention that Grimes’ prediction that CHD risk factors in generations born after the
1950s are somehow be different isn’t shown in observational nor clinical trial data. Nor is
the claim that CHD prediction charts “outdated” being backed up evidence. Etc. etc.

But yes, I do recommend that everyone read the paper. It’ll be a good exercise in critical
reading – and a good reminder that just because a paper can get published doesn’t mean it’s
worth that much.

## About Me

**Welcome to Doc’s Opinion.**
My name is **Axel F. Sigurdsson, MD, PhD, FACC**, and I’m the writer and editor of this blog.

I’m a practicing cardiologist in Reykjavík, Iceland, with a deep commitment to making medical
science more accessible—bridging the gap between complex research and practical understanding.

> **I write to bridge the distance between medical science and everyday life—because good medicine
> should be understood, not just practiced.**

## Clinical Background

I practice cardiology at the **Reykjavík Heart Center (Hjartamiðstöðin)**, a private heart clinic in
the Reykjavík area, and at **Myndgreining Hjartaverndar** (*The Imaging Center of the Icelandic
Heart Association*), where I specialize in interpreting **cardiovascular and coronary CT scans**.

I am a **Fellow of the American College of Cardiology (FACC)** and a member of both the **Icelandic
Society of Cardiology** and the **Swedish Society of Cardiology**. I also served as **President of
the Icelandic Cardiac Society**.

In addition to cardiology, I’m a licensed **Aviation Medical Examiner**, and I served as **Medical
Director for Icelandair** from 2004 to 2019.

## Education and Training

I earned my medical degree from the **University of Iceland** in 1984 and moved to **Sweden** for
postgraduate training in **internal medicine and cardiology** at **Sahlgrenska/Östra University
Hospital in Gothenburg**.

In **1993**, I completed my **PhD in Clinical Physiology** at the **University of Gothenburg**. My
thesis focused on:

> *“Neurohormonal Activation in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction or Chronic Congestive
> Heart Failure – With Special Reference to Treatment with ACE Inhibitors.”*

From 1995 to 1996, I completed a **clinical fellowship in interventional cardiology** at the **Royal
Jubilee Hospital** in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada.

Over the course of my career, I’ve authored and co-authored more than **100 scientific articles,
abstracts, and book chapters** in international journals and textbooks.

## About the Blog: Doc’s Opinion

I launched *Doc’s Opinion* in the spring of **2012** to offer thoughtful, evidence-based commentary
on **cardiovascular health**, **lifestyle medicine**, and **clinical science**. The blog is grounded
in the principles of **evidence-based medicine**, but it’s also shaped by curiosity, skepticism, and
a desire to connect medical knowledge with real life.

While the core focus includes:
* **Cardiovascular disease** and prevention
* **Lipidology** and cholesterol metabolism
* **Healthy lifestyle**, nutrition, and risk reduction
* **Patient education** and clinical insight

—I also write across disciplines. Many articles explore the wider **cultural, historical, and
psychological dimensions** of medicine: how guidelines are formed, how industry shapes science, how
wellness trends affect behavior, and how we think about health in the context of time, power, and
mortality. Some essays are reflective and personal. Others are investigative, analytical, or
narrative-driven. My aim is to challenge assumptions, clarify confusion, and bring depth to the
conversation around health.

A special feature of the blog is *The Heart of Power*—a historical series exploring the medical
lives of U.S. presidents. Blending biography with clinical insight, these stories examine how
illness shaped leadership, how health was concealed or weaponized, and how medicine and politics
have long been entangled in the highest office. It’s a lens on history through the pulse of power.

> literature and human experience.**

**Informative. Trustworthy. Accessible.**
That’s what I strive for in every post.

Community-acquired infections are contracted outside of healthcare settings, significantly impacting daily life. They range from mild illnesses to severe diseases such as pneumonia and meningitis.

Determining the exact cause of gastrointestinal symptoms can be challenging. Delays in diagnosis and treatment may result in serious complications, including abdominal catastrophes.

Gout is the most common form of inflammatory arthritis. Once called the "disease of kings," gout can result from holiday-related overindulgence in certain foods and beverages.

Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a prevalent substance-abuse condition that affects every organ system.

## We lead the NHS in England to deliver high quality services for all

If you are looking for information about health conditions and NHS services please visit
[NHS.uk][16].

[My Planned Care][17] gives you advice and support while you wait and helps you to prepare for your
hospital consultation, treatment, or surgery.

[NHS league tables][18] provide a view of how NHS trusts are performing in key services including
urgent and emergency care, elective services, mental health and more.

[[Doctor examining a patient]][19]

## [The best of the NHS][20]

Every day, NHS colleagues across the country are delivering outstanding care in new and innovative
ways. Discover some of the [best work happening in the NHS][21] right now.

[[A nurse stands by a hospital bed talking to a patient]][22]

## [Medium Term Planning Framework - delivering change together 2026/27 to 2028/29][23]

The [Medium Term Planning Framework – delivering change together 2026/27 to 2028/29][24] is the
NHS’s most ambitious plan in a generation, setting out how waiting times will be dramatically
reduced and local care restored over the next 3 years while resetting the foundations to deliver the
10 Year Health Plan.

### [Digital transformation][25]

Helping health and care professionals communicate better.

### [Elective care][26]

How we are improving experience and giving people choice and control for elective care services.

### [Workforce][27]

How we can put the NHS workforce on a sustainable footing and meet future challenges.

### [Mental health][28]

Improving outcomes and experiences of people with mental health problems.

### [Integrated care][29]

Giving people the support they need and removing disjointed care.

### [Cancer][30]

Making sure everyone with cancer receives care, support and treatment.

### [Urgent and emergency care][31]

Ensuring patients get the right care whenever they need it.

### [Primary care][32]

Offering patients a wider choice of personalised health services.

### [Health inequalities improvement][33]

Tackling health inequalities and advancing equality and diversity across the NHS.

### [NHS IMPACT][34]

Delivering continuous improvement across the NHS.

### [NHS @home][35]

Providing better connected, more personalised care in homes and care homes.

  CiteScore measures the average citations received per peer-reviewed document. CiteScore values are
  based on citation counts in a range of four years to peer-reviewed documents published in the same

## About

### ESMO Open

[[Cover Image - ESMO Open, Volume 11, Issue 7]][78]

*ESMO Open* is the European Society for Medical Oncology's online-only, peer-reviewed open access
journal, dedicated to publishing high-quality medical research and educational content from all
disciplines of oncology, with a focus on innovative clinical and translational cancer research. The
Journal aims to maximize industry networks to curate and disseminate preclinical or translational
data. We hope to bridge the gap between basic research and clinical applications, facilitating the
translation of groundbreaking discoveries into tangible advancements in cancer care. Our platform
will serve as a catalyst for innovation, nurturing the dialogue between academia, industry, and
clinical practice.

### ESMO

[ESMO  Opens in new window][79]   is the European Society for Medical Oncology. Representing over
50,000 members globally, ESMO is a reference for oncology education and information.

Founded in 1975, ESMO has European roots with a global reach. Home for all oncology stakeholders,
ESMO connects professionals with diverse expertise and experience. Its education and information
resources support an integrated multi-professional approach to cancer care, from a medical oncology
perspective.

ESMO seeks to erase boundaries in cancer care, whether between countries or specialities, and pursue
